item.title: Navruz in the Village
item.summary: A friend retells Aziz's story about making sumalak at his grandmother's house for Navruz.
item.transcript_text: Last week my friend Aziz told me about his Navruz holiday. He and his parents drove to his grandmother's village near Samarkand. The journey took about four hours because the roads were very busy. When they arrived, all the neighbours were in the garden. They were making sumalak in a huge pot over a fire. Aziz said that sumalak is made from young wheat, and people cook it all night. Everyone took turns to stir it, and they sang songs and told stories. Aziz stirred the pot until two o'clock in the morning, and then he fell asleep. In the morning, the sumalak was sweet and brown. His grandmother gave a small bowl to every family in the street. Aziz says it was the best Navruz of his life, and next year he wants to take me with him.
